newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: BASF plans two new plants in Manila, Seoul.
newsitem.headline: BASF plans two new plants in Manila, Seoul.

text.p: Germany's BASF is planning to set up two new acrylate dispersions plants in the Philippines and South Korea, each with a yearly capacity of 25,000 tonnes, a statement from the company said on Friday.
With this move, the company said it will further strengthen its position in Southeast Asia. It already has production plants in China, Indonesia, Australia, India, Japan, and Pakistan.
Acrylate dispersions are used in the paint and adhesives industry.
BASF Philippine head Jaime Mendoza said the two plants will be sourcing its raw materials, principally acrylic acid and acrylic esters from BASF's own plants in Asia.
Letters of intent were signed recently for the construction of new plants in China and Malaysia that will produce acrylic acids, he said.

In the Philippines, Mendoza said the new acyrlate dispersions plant is expected to cost 20 million marks. It will start commercial operations in the first quarter of 1999. The plant will be located in Canlubang, Laguna province south of Manila.
Mendoza told Reuters the plant in South Korea is also expected to cost 20 million marks and will be onstream almost at the same time as the Philippine plant.
